title: These Herefordshire sites all have chilling ghost stories... and you can visit!
excerpt: Halloween is fast approaching and there are plenty of spots with a spooky past in Herefordshire to explore in October.
content:
Halloween is fast approaching and there are plenty of spots with a spooky past in Herefordshire.

Whether its a haunted hotel or a castle, here are five of the most haunted historic buildings in the county.

The Green Dragon Hotel

The Green Dragon Hotel stands in the heart of Hereford and has long been associated with ghostly activity.

Dating back several centuries, the building’s age and history have fuelled stories of unexplained footsteps, mysterious figures and strange noises heard by staff and guests.

Legend suggests former residents and visitors may still linger in its corridors, with reports describing shadowy apparitions in upper-floor rooms.

Croft Castle

Croft Castle is near Leominster and is known for its beautiful grounds, centuries of history and paranormal tales.

Local legend says several ghosts roam the castle, including figures linked to the Croft family, who occupied the estate for generations.

Visitors and staff have reported unexplained sounds and an eerie presence in certain rooms.

St Briavels Castle

St Briavels Castle is just across the border, in an area closely linked with Herefordshire history.

The medieval fortress is said to be haunted by several spirits, including the ghost of a young girl whose cries have reportedly been heard within its walls.

Its dark prison cells, ancient stone passageways and turbulent history have helped build its chilling reputation.

Goodrich Castle

Goodrich Castle overlooks the River Wye and is one of Herefordshire’s most dramatic medieval landmarks.

The castle played a significant role during the English Civil War, and local folklore claims some people who perished during conflicts there still haunt the ruins.

Visitors have reported strange sensations, unexplained sounds and an unsettling feeling around parts of the fortress.

Hellens Manor

Hellens Manor is in the village of Much Marcle and is widely regarded as one of England’s most haunted historic houses.

Dating back to the 12th century, the manor has accumulated ghostly legends, including one involving the alleged ghost of a woman known as Hetty Walwyn.

She is said to appear in one of the manor’s rooms, while mysterious footsteps, unexplained noises and spectral figures have also been reported.

These buildings continue to attract interest through their history, atmosphere and enduring supernatural legends.
